# `Q-2-9` — HTML Element Auto-converted

> An HTML element in markdown text was auto-converted to a
> raw-HTML inline. Warning only.

## What this means

When Quarto encounters raw HTML (like `<span>` or a custom tag)
inside markdown, it does not reject the element; it converts it
to a Pandoc `RawInline` with format `html` and emits this warning.
The output is identical to what an explicit raw-HTML attribute
would produce, but the warning calls attention to the implicit
conversion.

## Why this happens

The pattern shows up whenever raw HTML appears in markdown text:

- A custom HTML element copied from elsewhere.
- A `<span>` or `<div>` used for styling.
- Embedded widget markup.

## How to fix

The warning does not block the build, so no action is strictly
required. To silence the warning, mark the snippet explicitly as
raw HTML using Pandoc's raw-attribute form:

```markdown
`<custom-tag>content</custom-tag>`{=html}
```

This is also the form Quarto recommends — it makes the intent
explicit and is portable across formats.
